sources.title: St. Kitts and Nevis Third National Communication to the UNFCCC
sources.organization: Government of St. Kitts and Nevis, Ministry of Sustainable Development, Environment, Climate Action and Constituency Empowerment
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate vulnerability, sector impacts, adaptation readiness and observations reported through November 2024; includes climate projections.
sources.methodology: Government TNC with vulnerability assessment, sector review, stakeholder survey and cited climate projections.
sources.limitations: Government self-report; projections vary by source, and some impacts are qualitative and not site-specific.

sources.title: CORVI Risk Profile: Basseterre, St. Kitts and Nevis
sources.organization: Stimson Center Environmental Security Program, with TaiwanICDF, Taiwan Ocean Affairs Council and Government of St. Kitts and Nevis
sources.temporal_coverage: Basseterre climate and ocean risks and resilience planning as assessed in 2021-2022, with retrospective observations.
sources.methodology: CORVI city profile using 96 indicators, data, 60 expert surveys, 21 interviews and desk research.
sources.limitations: City-level empirical data were limited; survey, interview and data findings diverged. Scores are relative to regional cities.

sources.title: Report of the vulnerability and capacity assessments in coastal and fishing communities in Saint Kitts and Nevis
sources.organization: Caribbean Natural Resources Institute (CANARI), with the Department of Marine Resources, Government of Saint Kitts and Nevis
sources.temporal_coverage: Participatory assessments conducted in selected coastal and fishing communities mainly in 2020; report published in 2022.
sources.methodology: Three-site participatory photo-journaling, interviews and fisheries value-chain assessment.
sources.limitations: Small purposive samples; participant findings are not representative.

sources.title: Final Workshops Held for GCF Readiness 4 Project in St. Kitts and Nevis
sources.organization: St. Kitts and Nevis Information Service (SKNIS), Government of St. Kitts and Nevis
sources.temporal_coverage: Outputs reported at the conclusion of the three-year GCF Readiness 4 project in January-February 2025.
sources.methodology: Government news report summarizing project workshops and outputs reported by the implementing partners.
sources.limitations: Official project summary, not an independent evaluation of whether systems are operational or outcomes sustained.

sources.title: WSD Advances Water Security and Reliability Initiatives Amid Climate Change Challenges
sources.organization: Ministry of Public Infrastructure, Energy, and Utilities, Government of St. Kitts and Nevis
sources.temporal_coverage: Water-service conditions and department initiatives reported in June 2026, with projected future well and pipeline capacity.
sources.methodology: Ministry news report summarizing a Water Services Department manager's June 16, 2026 progress presentation.
sources.limitations: Government report of service and project status; future supply volumes are projections, not verified delivery outcomes.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 193-194, Table 4.7, row 'Increase in the intensity and frequency of stronger storms (>Cat 3)'.
claims.paraphrase: For stronger storms, the TNC lists possible homelessness or displacement among poor people and possible sexual assault or GBV among displaced or sheltered people.
claims.scenario: Qualitative projection; Table 4.7 gives no row-specific emissions scenario, period or locality.
claims.limitations: Qualitative projection, not observed incidence or organized conflict; no local estimate.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: TNC links stronger storms, displacement or sheltering and possible sexual assault/GBV.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 182-183, 'Infrastructure & Settlements' subsection of Climate Impacts and Hotspots.
claims.paraphrase: Most urban settlements are on low-lying coastal plains; TNC names Basseterre, Sandy Point, Charlestown and Newcastle.
claims.limitations: National description; no town-specific exposure estimates.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 198-199, 'Institutional Capacity & Human Resources' and 'Information, Technology and Data Systems'.
claims.paraphrase: Nevis data and downscaled-information gaps limit community-scale planning; Sandy Point and school warning systems exist, but health has none.
institutions: St. Kitts and Nevis Meteorological Services
claims.limitations: Report does not evaluate local warning reach or performance.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 2-3, Summary Findings; p. 6, 'Geology/Water' and 'Climate' category discussion.
claims.paraphrase: Basseterre, home to about 27% of the population, scores medium-high on fisheries, coastal ecosystems, water and economic risks; heat and hurricanes are prominent indicators.
claims.limitations: Relative city scores combine ecological, financial and political risks; they are not climate-attributable loss measures.

claims.paraphrase: The report states 51% of renewable freshwater was withdrawn, 31 wells supplied 70% of potable water, and 2017 drought brought severe rationing; Basseterre Valley holds the main aquifer.
claims.limitations: Withdrawal and well-supply figures are report-era, not current measurements.

claims.locator: Printed p. 14, 'Economics' discussion of informal economy and resilience planning.
claims.paraphrase: Basseterre interviews identify difficulty reaching informal workers with policy; their limited institutional integration impedes inclusion in resilience planning and recovery.
institutions: Government of St. Kitts and Nevis
claims.limitations: Reported inclusion constraint, not evidence of conflict or violence restricting adaptation.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 29-30, Dieppe Bay geography and climate-change impacts; pp. 17-18, fisheries infrastructure findings.
claims.paraphrase: Dieppe Bay participants described homes, buildings, landing facilities and roads as exposed on a windward coast with little setback; erosion affects the settlement and coastal protection.
claims.limitations: Community observations, not measured hazard survey.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 28-30, Dieppe Bay fisheries context and key climate impacts.
claims.paraphrase: Hurricane Irma destroyed the Capisterre cooperative in 2017; it remained unrepaired at the 2020 assessment, leaving fishers without storage or processing space.
claims.limitations: Status is as of the 2020 assessment.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 41-42, Sandy Point photo-journaling findings.
claims.paraphrase: Sandy Point participants linked Pump Bay erosion and past storms that damaged the cooperative and pier with difficulty hauling and securing fishing boats.
claims.limitations: Community observation; Belle Tete sand mining is noted separately as a non-climate pressure.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 51-53, Newcastle Bay findings; p. 59, Newcastle adaptation priorities table.
claims.paraphrase: Newcastle Bay fishers reported erosion and storm damage to the landing site and pier; the Foundation organized participation and UNDP/GEF grants supported lockers, but further facilities were requested.
claims.limitations: Participatory report; does not evaluate locker performance.

claims.locator: Government article sections 'Highlights of the Workshops' and 'Project Conclusion'.
claims.paraphrase: At the 2025 project close, the government reported updated emergency plans, an operational and training framework for NEMA and NDMD, an impact-based multi-hazard warning framework, a storm-surge atlas and climate-data tools.
institutions: St. Kitts and Nevis Meteorological Services
claims.limitations: The report describes project outputs and handover, not independent validation of operational readiness or ongoing use.

claims.locator: Article sections 'The Basseterre Desalination Plant' and 'Enhancements in St. Peters'.
claims.paraphrase: The ministry reports the Basseterre desalination plant began service in February 2026, restoring round-the-clock water for about 20,000 customers; at publication, a pipeline and pump for higher-elevation Saint Peters were installed and being tested.
claims.limitations: Service figures and installation status are reported by the ministry; the Saint Peters system was still under testing, not confirmed operational.

claims.locator: Article sections 'Groundwater Drilling' and 'Construction of 500 000 Gallon Water Tank in Cayon'.
claims.paraphrase: The ministry projects ten candidate wells could yield up to four million gallons daily and meet demand through 2040; drilling at Saddlers began in January 2026.
claims.scenario: The article projects aggregate candidate-site capacity through 2040; no climate scenario or model is stated.
claims.limitations: Only Saddlers drilling had begun; aggregate well yield is prospective.

search_audit.query: St Kitts and Nevis parish coastal fishing community climate vulnerability erosion flooding drought official assessment
search_audit.outcome: Read the government TNC, city CORVI profile and participatory coastal/fisheries VCA. Verified named findings for Basseterre, Dieppe Bay, Sandy Point/Pump Bay and Newcastle Bay; evidence is not a complete island-wide local comparison.

search_audit.query: St Kitts Nevis climate storm drought violence conflict displacement gender based violence social tension primary report
search_audit.outcome: The TNC qualitatively projects storm-related displacement/sheltering and possible sexual assault/GBV; this is not observed or a conflict finding. CORVI reports social tension and civil unrest as low relative-risk indicators and does not attribute them to climate.

search_audit.query: St Kitts Nevis conflict violence displacement land access constraints climate adaptation institutional primary source
search_audit.outcome: No primary source-stated organized conflict or violence constraint on climate adaptation was verified. Sources report informal-worker inclusion and institutional/data-resource constraints, without linking those constraints to FCV.

search_audit.query: St Kitts Nevis NEMA meteorological early warning water drought resilience capacity project official
search_audit.outcome: TNC records existing and missing warning/data capacity; the 2025 project article lists plans, tools and training outputs; the 2026 ministry report gives water-service changes and candidate well projections. Project reporting is not independent performance evaluation.

gaps: No verified country-specific source-stated climate-change-to-organized-conflict or organized-conflict-to-adaptation-constraint pathway was located. The TNC's storm-displacement/GBV pathway is qualitative and projected.
The 2023 Voluntary National Review PDF surfaced in indexed search, but direct open returned HTTP 403; indexed text was not used as evidence.
Participatory coastal findings focus on three selected fishing communities and small workshop samples; these do not support representative island-wide prevalence estimates.
Local information was strongest for Basseterre and selected coastal fishing communities; evidence on climate vulnerability and adaptation in other parishes is thinner.
